name: perf_sprint_ivf_hnsw
method: criterion A/B via git-stash of the two optimized source files (ivf.rs, hnsw.rs); baseline run first (cooler start), then optimized compared against the named baseline. 3s warmup + 100 samples (search) / 20 samples (build) per criterion defaults.

hardware.note: Laptop / unplugged-class thermal envelope. Back-to-back heavy criterion runs cause thermal throttling that contaminates the FASTER benches run early in a sequence (see caveats).

ivf_search_diverse_queries_cold.comment: 20k vectors, n_lists=256, n_probe=16, k=10, 512 distinct cycling queries (cold-memory access — the realistic regime; a single repeated query is cache-warm and invalid for measuring prefetch).

d128.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE — thermal noise (huge CI; contradicts warm-run -12%)

d256.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE — thermal noise (huge CI; warm run showed -12%)

d768.verdict: CLEAN WIN — tight CI; most cold-memory-bound dimension

hnsw_build_highd.comment: Concurrent build, 3k vectors, d=256, m=16, ef_construction=200.

nf4_encode_neon.comment: WS-C: NEON SIMD nibble search (15-way threshold sum, 4-wide) vs scalar nibble. Batch encode 2k vectors, pure-compute (low thermal noise).

trustworthy_conclusions: WS-D HNSW build: ~15-18% faster at d=256, consistent across cosine AND l2 — exceeds the plan's 5-15% estimate. (An earlier single run showed cosine +35% / l2 flat, which was thermal noise, not a real regression — confirmed by this consistent re-measure.)
WS-A flat store + prefetch: -21% IVF search at d=768 (cold), the most memory-latency-bound case, validating the flat-layout + prefetch thesis where it matters most.

The d128/d256 'regressions' are environmental thermal noise, NOT a real prefetch cost: a prefetch-overhead regression would hit d768 HARDEST (48 prfm/vec vs 8 at d128) — but d768 IMPROVED most and d128/d256 had ±20-30% CIs. The warm microbench had shown d256 -12%.
caveats_and_followups: This M3 laptop is thermally noisy for sub-500us benches run back-to-back; d128/d256 need a controlled re-run (AC power, cooldown between baseline/optimized, or a server-class machine) before claiming a number.
The single-query tight-loop microbench is cache-warm and INVALID for prefetch evaluation; always cycle diverse queries (done here) so the working set exceeds LLC.
WS-A memory win (removing N per-vector Vec headers, ~24 B/vec) is not captured here — measure RSS at 1M scale separately.
